## Benchmark suites {#bench}

`bench/instances/*.txt` hold the instances that every solver is timed on. One instance per line,
`name|arguments`, where the arguments are `zeno` instance options and `@DATA@` stands for
`bench/instances/data/` (data files in the [2-line format](model.qmd#data-files)). Lines starting
with `#` are comments.

{{< include _suites.md >}}

The tables below list every instance with the size of its front, from `zeno`'s baseline
(`bench/baselines/zeno/apple-m4-max/zeno.json`). The timings of every solver on them are on the
[results page](../results.qmd), and their fronts are plotted on the
[instances page](index.qmd).

{{< include _suites-detail.md >}}

To time a solver over the suites ([`bench/README.md`](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/bench/README.md)):

```sh
bench/tools/run_suite.py --exe build/bench/zeno \
    --suite bench/instances/regimes.txt --suite bench/instances/families.txt \
    --timeout 30 --repetitions 3 --machine apple-m4-max --out zeno.json
bench/tools/check_regression.py baseline.json zeno.json [--threshold 0.10]
```

## Golden instances {#golden}

`tests/golden/instances.txt` lists 27 tiny symmetric instances (`name|arguments`, `@DATA@` for
`tests/golden/data/`). Their fronts, in `tests/golden/fronts/<name>.front` as `cost makespan`
lines by increasing cost, were computed by the brute-force oracle `zenoOracle`
(`tests/oracle/bruteForce.hpp`). The oracle enumerates every PPP, every beta set, and every
assignment and order of flights to planes, and simulates the waiting exactly. It is exponential
($t \le 5$; `n = 6 t = 6 p = 2` already takes minutes).

{{< include _golden.md >}}

For every instance, CTest checks that the front of `zeno` equals the golden front
(`tests/golden/checkFront.cmake`) and that `zeno check` accepts its certificate
(`checkCertificate.cmake`). Pairs known to fail go in `tests/golden/known-bugs.txt`, currently
none; a listed pair that passes fails the suite. To regenerate the fronts:

```sh
tests/golden/regenerate.sh build/release/zenoOracle
```

Instances of note:

- `lpt-counterexample`: $d = (6, 10)$, $c = (40, 20)$, $t = 5$, $p = 2$. The point (260, 60) is
  Pareto-optimal, but scheduling its landings longest-first onto the least-loaded plane gives
  makespan 68. Its front is also proved in Lean by the kernel alone
  (`Examples.lptCounterexample_front`, [§5](../proofs.qmd#node-s5)).
- `p3-first-counterexample`: $d = (1, 3)$, $c = (9, 5)$, $t = 4$, $p = 2$. The point (42, 12)
  needs the plane making the drop-off to also take the long crossing.
- `nodup-best-plan` and `trailing-newline`: $d = (1, 9)$, $c = (4, 1)$, $t = 5$, $p = 3$, read from
  a file without and with a trailing blank line, which must not change the instance.
- The first sixteen use the default generator, including the $n = t$, $p = 2$ instances (front
  sizes 5, 10, 17, [known fronts](known-fronts.qmd#table1)); the next seven use other families and
  scales. Golden names encode generator flags; the arguments column is what `zeno` runs.

## Lean test sets

- `lean/test/certificates/accepted/` and `rejected/`: certificates written by `zeno`, and corrupted
  copies with a comment saying what was broken (a wrong cost or duration, a broken route,
  non-monotone points, a missing point, a `forest` gap relabelled `relaxed`, a missing assumption,
  a truncated file, and version 2 cases such as the Proposition 6.5 instance without its point
  (14, 74)). `bash lean/test/run.sh` checks each against its expected verdict.
- `lean/test/instances/`: random instances for the end-to-end run (`lean/test/e2e.sh`), five of
  them with a `forest` gap.
- `lean/test/front-regimes.list`: the three suite regimes on which `zeno-front` is compared with
  `zeno front` in CI.
